subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should external source-channel turns move to a safer default that suppresses automatic intermediate/final-looking text during tool-running turns, including direct chats and cron announce delivery, or should stricter delivery remain opt-in via existing visible-reply settings?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the permanent fix changes a user-visible delivery/security boundary and can break setups that intentionally rely on automatic bare-text replies.

options.title: Safer external default
options.body: Make external tool-running source turns private unless output is final-only or sent via the message tool, with an explicit opt-out or migration guidance for legacy automatic replies.

options.title: Opt-in stricter mode only
options.body: Keep automatic replies as the default and land only narrower filters or docs around `messages.visibleReplies`, minimizing upgrade breakage but leaving more leak risk on default installs.

options.title: Split by surface
options.body: Keep ordinary direct chats automatic while making shared rooms, cron announce, and ambient contexts message-tool-only or final-only by default.

recommendation.title: Safer external default
recommendation.body: Make external tool-running source turns private unless output is final-only or sent via the message tool, with an explicit opt-out or migration guidance for legacy automatic replies.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged visible-reply policy work is the closest owner-history signal for this delivery boundary decision.
